ClinicalDocument.title: SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD — Progress Note 2 — Focused Visit (Follow-up) — Jean-Jacques Rousseau — True-date frame: synthetic events are moved into the patient's historical lifetime. Codes, instruments, and treatments remain modern and are anachronistic.

code.originalText: Psychiatry consultation and review of the urethral imaging and cystoscopy

text.paragraph: Results of the urethral imaging and cystoscopy; psychiatry consultation today. [S]

Mr. Rousseau returns two weeks after presenting with long-held beliefs of a plot against him, poor sleep, and difficulty passing urine. He saw Dr. Lindqvist-Hale of psychiatry this morning. The kidney and bladder ultrasound eleven days ago showed normal kidneys without hydronephrosis and a thickened, trabeculated bladder. Five days ago the urology team performed a retrograde urethrogram, a voiding cystourethrogram, and a flexible cystoscopy: a dense, ring-like narrowing 1.5 cm long in the proximal bulbar urethra, with a lumen of about 8 French, which the scope could not pass; the meatus is normal, with no hypospadias, and the bladder neck opens normally. He has not used his urethral sounds since the first visit, as advised; his stream is no worse and he has not been unable to pass urine. He read the reports himself and brought written questions. He still sleeps about four hours and spends much of the day thinking about the people he believes are working against him, and he has stopped opening letters from people he suspects. He has had no thoughts of suicide or of harming anyone and has made no plan to confront anyone. [S]

S — Synthetic modern diagnosis. His beliefs and conduct are documented (D); calling them a paranoid delusion is a retrospective interpretation (R), made difficult by the real persecution he suffered.

list.item:
Delusional disorder, persecutory type (F22). Psychiatry confirms delusional disorder, persecutory type: fixed, non-bizarre persecutory beliefs for about nine years, without hallucinations, disorganized speech or behavior, or negative symptoms, so schizophrenia is excluded; the beliefs are held with delusional conviction rather than as the suspicious attitudes of paranoid personality disorder; the mild depressive symptoms (PHQ-9 8) followed the beliefs and are not a mood episode with psychotic features; and the normal neurological examination, MoCA 28, normal laboratory tests, and absence of substance use make a medical, neurocognitive, or substance cause unlikely, so brain imaging is not needed now. The presenting concern is resolved into this diagnosis. Risk to himself and others is low. He has the capacity to make decisions about his treatment. [S]
Cognitive behavioral therapy for psychosis with the clinic psychologist, first session next week, aimed at distress, worry, and sleep rather than at disproving the beliefs; he accepts it as help for his sleep and his peace of mind.
Aripiprazole 5 mg daily offered, with its likely benefits and side effects; he declined it today and the offer stays open, as Dr. Lindqvist-Hale advised.
Safety plan reviewed and unchanged; the 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline and the clinic number confirmed.
Copies of today's notes given to him, as he asked.

Bulbar urethral stricture, 1.5 cm (N35.812). A short, dense bulbar stricture that has been treated, in effect, by repeated dilation for decades; the presenting urinary concern is resolved into this diagnosis. Kidney function is normal and there is no hydronephrosis. The urology team has explained dilation, internal urethrotomy, self-catheterization, and urethroplasty; because the stricture has recurred after years of dilation, urethroplasty is recommended over further endoscopic treatment. He wants time to read about the choices. [S]
Continue urethral rest: no sounds or self-dilation; come in the same day if he cannot pass urine.
Urology clinic to discuss the operation with him in three weeks.

Right inguinal hernia (K40.90). Reducible and minimally symptomatic. [S]
Watchful waiting; review after the stricture is treated.
